classification.difficultyReason: Interpret being behind a race record as a time difference and subtract the record from each finishing time, retaining seconds.

content.prompt: Three girls ran first, second and third in a 100 m race, with times of 12.30 s, 12.63 s and 13.16 s, respectively. If the national record time for this race is 11.47 s, how far behind the record is each of these girls?

answer.worked:
Align the decimal points and subtract the record time from each finishing time.

$$\begin{align*}12.30-11.47&=0.83\text{ s}\\12.63-11.47&=1.16\text{ s}\\13.16-11.47&=1.69\text{ s}\end{align*}$$

The first, second and third girls were 0.83 s, 1.16 s and 1.69 s behind the record, respectively.
